production.note: US model years. Start: GM's 2001 Corvette release (dated July 1, 2000) introduces the Z06 as new for the 2001 model year, so the first cars were built in calendar 2000. End: GM's April 2003 release calls 2004 "the final chapter in the C5 era" (source gm-2004-commemorative-release), and the GM Media specification table for 2004 still lists the Z06 (source gm-2004-corvette-specs).

body.note: Fixed-roof hardtop only; GM lists it as "Z06 (hardtop)", based on the former hardtop model.

transmission.note: The M12 six-speed manual is the only transmission offered on the Z06 (also stated in GM's 2001 and 2004 releases, sources gm-2001-corvette-overview and gm-2004-corvette-specs).

powerHp.note: 2002 to 2004 rating. Quote: "The new LS6 V8 delivers 405 horsepower at 6000 rpm"; spec table Z06 column: "405 @ 6000 rpm". The 2001 model was rated 385 hp. Quote (source gm-2001-corvette-overview): "The LS-6 engine delivers 385 hp @ 6000 rpm". Reference year is 2002 because the 405 hp rating applied to three of the four model years. The GM Media table for 2004 gives the same "405 / 302 @ 6000" (source gm-2004-corvette-specs).

weightLb.note: Manufacturer curb weight, standard 2002 Z06 (hardtop, six-speed manual, the only configuration). Quote, spec table Z06 column: "Curb Weight (lbs/kg): 3118 / 1414". The GM Media table for 2004 gives the same "3118 / 1414" (source gm-2004-corvette-specs).

discrepancies.reason: Model year and option package: the museum page describes the 2004 Commemorative Edition Z06, an optioned car with a carbon-fiber hood (GM: 10.6 lb lighter than the standard hood), and gives no origin for its 3,086 lb figure. GM's own tables give 3,118 lb for the standard Z06 in both 2002 and 2004.
discrepancies.resolution: Used GM's 3,118 lb for the standard 2002 Z06. A weight for an optioned car is not used, and the museum figure is not a manufacturer or major-publication figure.
